terms.title: Account Lifecycle
terms.summary: The governed process that creates, updates, and retires Nexus accounts, ensuring every change is validated by the Iroha Virtual Machine and the hosting data space's policy.
terms.definition: The governed process that creates, updates, and retires Nexus accounts, ensuring every change is validated by the Iroha Virtual Machine and the hosting data space's policy.

terms.title: AccountId
terms.summary: A typed Norito pointer that uniquely references a Nexus account, including network, data-space UUID, domain, name, and checksum fields for deterministic validation.
terms.definition: A typed Norito pointer that uniquely references a Nexus account, including network, data-space UUID, domain, name, and checksum fields for deterministic validation.

terms.title: Action
terms.summary: The executable portion of a trigger or automation, defining which Iroha Special Instructions or Kotodama call should run once the associated condition is satisfied and budget is available.
terms.definition: The executable portion of a trigger or automation, defining which Iroha Special Instructions or Kotodama call should run once the associated condition is satisfied and budget is available.

terms.title: Activation Slot
terms.summary: The ledger slot pre-scheduled in a governed manifest where an approved runtime upgrade or configuration change becomes active across all lanes.
terms.definition: The ledger slot pre-scheduled in a governed manifest where an approved runtime upgrade or configuration change becomes active across all lanes.

terms.title: Admission
terms.summary: The transaction intake stage where gateways and validators enforce roles, quotas, fees, and Start-Time Fair Queuing so only policy-compliant work enters execution.
terms.definition: The transaction intake stage where gateways and validators enforce roles, quotas, fees, and Start-Time Fair Queuing so only policy-compliant work enters execution.

terms.title: Aggregation
terms.summary: The bundling phase that collects each data space's state roots, proofs, and data-availability artifacts into lane blocks prior to consensus.
terms.definition: The bundling phase that collects each data space's state roots, proofs, and data-availability artifacts into lane blocks prior to consensus.

terms.title: Assembly
terms.summary: One of the two SORA Parliament chambers, representing the wider stakeholder base with stake-weighted or one-person-one-vote selection and on-chain proposal rights.
terms.definition: One of the two SORA Parliament chambers, representing the wider stakeholder base with stake-weighted or one-person-one-vote selection and on-chain proposal rights.

terms.title: AssetDefinitionId
terms.summary: A typed handle that points to an asset schema within a data space, allowing contracts to reference assets without ambiguous string parsing.
terms.definition: A typed handle that points to an asset schema within a data space, allowing contracts to reference assets without ambiguous string parsing.

terms.title: Attestations
terms.summary: Signed statements - typically using ML-DSA-87 - that certify new data spaces, DA proofs, or governance actions before the network accepts them.
terms.definition: Signed statements - typically using ML-DSA-87 - that certify new data spaces, DA proofs, or governance actions before the network accepts them.

terms.title: Attesters
terms.summary: Specialized actors who verify erasure-coded shards and proofs, then issue DA certificates so validators can rely on the data without downloading everything.
terms.definition: Specialized actors who verify erasure-coded shards and proofs, then issue DA certificates so validators can rely on the data without downloading everything.

terms.title: Automation
terms.summary: Deterministic, on-ledger workflows composed of conditions, actions, and budgets that let operators schedule recurring payments or policy checks without off-chain bots.
terms.definition: Deterministic, on-ledger workflows composed of conditions, actions, and budgets that let operators schedule recurring payments or policy checks without off-chain bots.

terms.title: Bech32 Format
terms.summary: The human-readable string encoding used for Nexus account addresses, derived from the canonical binary layout and protected with a Blake2b checksum.
terms.definition: The human-readable string encoding used for Nexus account addresses, derived from the canonical binary layout and protected with a Blake2b checksum.

terms.title: Blake2b
terms.summary: The fast hash function used for tasks like leader selection, account checksums, and pseudo-randomness inside the SUMERAGI pipeline.
terms.definition: The fast hash function used for tasks like leader selection, account checksums, and pseudo-randomness inside the SUMERAGI pipeline.

terms.title: Blinded CIDs
terms.summary: Obfuscated content identifiers within SoraNet that preserve privacy by hiding the underlying data reference while still allowing routing and settlement.
terms.definition: Obfuscated content identifiers within SoraNet that preserve privacy by hiding the underlying data reference while still allowing routing and settlement.

terms.title: Budget
terms.summary: The TEU and fee allowance assigned to a trigger or automation, ensuring it cannot consume unlimited compute or bandwidth.
terms.definition: The TEU and fee allowance assigned to a trigger or automation, ensuring it cannot consume unlimited compute or bandwidth.

terms.title: Canonical Primitives
terms.summary: The curated list of cryptographic algorithms (Poseidon2, DEEP-FRI, ML-DSA-87, etc.) that SORA Nexus mandates to keep security assumptions consistent across data spaces.
terms.definition: The curated list of cryptographic algorithms (Poseidon2, DEEP-FRI, ML-DSA-87, etc.) that SORA Nexus mandates to keep security assumptions consistent across data spaces.

terms.title: Circuit Breakers
terms.summary: Automated controls that throttle lane admission, message sizes, or DA limits when the system detects stress, preventing resource exhaustion.
terms.definition: Automated controls that throttle lane admission, message sizes, or DA limits when the system detects stress, preventing resource exhaustion.

terms.title: Circuit-Breaker State
terms.summary: The telemetry surface exposing which circuit breakers are engaged, letting operators observe throttling events and recovery in real time.
terms.definition: The telemetry surface exposing which circuit breakers are engaged, letting operators observe throttling events and recovery in real time.

terms.title: Collateralized Locks
terms.summary: Escrowed funds backing offline-offline vouchers, providing settlement guarantees until reconciliation clears or revokes the transfer.
terms.definition: Escrowed funds backing offline-offline vouchers, providing settlement guarantees until reconciliation clears or revokes the transfer.

terms.title: Commit Window
terms.summary: The bounded number of slots (Delta <= 2) within which SUMERAGI must finalize a proposal, ensuring predictable finality even under adversarial network conditions.
terms.definition: The bounded number of slots (Delta <= 2) within which SUMERAGI must finalize a proposal, ensuring predictable finality even under adversarial network conditions.

terms.title: Commitments
terms.summary: Cryptographic bindings (Merkle roots, Poseidon2 hashes) that tie execution traces, memory, or DA shards to a block so verifiers can audit them without re-running all computation.
terms.definition: Cryptographic bindings (Merkle roots, Poseidon2 hashes) that tie execution traces, memory, or DA shards to a block so verifiers can audit them without re-running all computation.

terms.title: Compute Lane
terms.summary: A dedicated lane that runs governed compute manifests - like SoraNet streaming or heavy analytics - without interfering with core transaction lanes.
terms.definition: A dedicated lane that runs governed compute manifests - like SoraNet streaming or heavy analytics - without interfering with core transaction lanes.

terms.title: ComputeManifest
terms.summary: The on-chain specification describing which workloads a compute lane accepts, how they're routed, and which data spaces they can access.
terms.definition: The on-chain specification describing which workloads a compute lane accepts, how they're routed, and which data spaces they can access.

terms.title: Condition
terms.summary: The predicate part of a trigger (time-based, event-based, or receipt-based) that must evaluate true before its actions consume TEU budget.
terms.definition: The predicate part of a trigger (time-based, event-based, or receipt-based) that must evaluate true before its actions consume TEU budget.

terms.title: Cross-Border Corridors
terms.summary: A highlighted use case where Nexus hosts multi-jurisdiction payment networks with deterministic policy enforcement and shared liquidity.
terms.definition: A highlighted use case where Nexus hosts multi-jurisdiction payment networks with deterministic policy enforcement and shared liquidity.

terms.title: Curve25519
terms.summary: The elliptic-curve key exchange primitive paired with Kyber768 in SoraNet's hybrid post-quantum handshake.
terms.definition: The elliptic-curve key exchange primitive paired with Kyber768 in SoraNet's hybrid post-quantum handshake.

terms.title: DA Certificates
terms.summary: Signed attestations from validators or attesters confirming that required data-availability samples were checked and can be reconstructed.
terms.definition: Signed attestations from validators or attesters confirming that required data-availability samples were checked and can be reconstructed.

terms.title: DA Sampling
terms.summary: The process of fetching a limited number of erasure-coded shards per data space in-slot to statistically guarantee recoverability without downloading entire envelopes.
terms.definition: The process of fetching a limited number of erasure-coded shards per data space in-slot to statistically guarantee recoverability without downloading entire envelopes.

terms.title: DA Sampling Budget
terms.summary: The governance cap (e.g., q_total <= 2048) on how many DA samples can be performed per slot so verification stays within hardware limits.
terms.definition: The governance cap (e.g., q_total <= 2048) on how many DA samples can be performed per slot so verification stays within hardware limits.

terms.title: DA Sampling Confidence
terms.summary: The probability, computed via combinatorics, that malicious withholding will be detected given the chosen sample count and committee size.
terms.definition: The probability, computed via combinatorics, that malicious withholding will be detected given the chosen sample count and committee size.

terms.title: Data Availability
terms.summary: The guarantee that every transaction's payload can be reconstructed by honest parties, even when the original submitter goes offline.
terms.definition: The guarantee that every transaction's payload can be reconstructed by honest parties, even when the original submitter goes offline.

terms.title: Data Availability Layer
terms.summary: The combined erasure-coding, sampling, proving, and attestation system that enforces data availability across public and private data spaces.
terms.definition: The combined erasure-coding, sampling, proving, and attestation system that enforces data availability across public and private data spaces.

terms.title: Data Envelope
terms.summary: The serialized bundle of transactions, proofs, and metadata that a data space contributes to a lane block before erasure coding.
terms.definition: The serialized bundle of transactions, proofs, and metadata that a data space contributes to a lane block before erasure coding.

terms.title: Data Space Directory
terms.summary: The on-chain registry mapping DSIDs to owners, routing endpoints, and policy metadata so gateways know how to handle each space.
terms.definition: The on-chain registry mapping DSIDs to owners, routing endpoints, and policy metadata so gateways know how to handle each space.

terms.title: Data Spaces
terms.summary: First-class, sovereignty-preserving partitions that allow different jurisdictions or applications to share the same ledger without sharing their private data.
terms.definition: First-class, sovereignty-preserving partitions that allow different jurisdictions or applications to share the same ledger without sharing their private data.

terms.title: DataSpaceId
terms.summary: A typed pointer that identifies which data space an account, asset, or instruction belongs to, enabling cross-space safety checks.
terms.definition: A typed pointer that identifies which data space an account, asset, or instruction belongs to, enabling cross-space safety checks.

terms.title: DEEP-FRI
terms.summary: The low-degree testing protocol inside FASTPQ STARK proofs that lets verifiers check massive execution traces with logarithmic work.
terms.definition: The low-degree testing protocol inside FASTPQ STARK proofs that lets verifiers check massive execution traces with logarithmic work.

terms.title: Deterministic Budgets
terms.summary: Governed resource ceilings - like TEU per lane or DA sample counts - that avoid nondeterministic scheduling and make performance predictable.
terms.definition: Governed resource ceilings - like TEU per lane or DA sample counts - that avoid nondeterministic scheduling and make performance predictable.

terms.title: Deterministic Runtime
terms.summary: The design principle of the IVM: no floating point, no non-deterministic syscalls, and explicit memory models so execution is bit-for-bit reproducible.
terms.definition: The design principle of the IVM: no floating point, no non-deterministic syscalls, and explicit memory models so execution is bit-for-bit reproducible.

terms.title: Developer Experience
terms.summary: The suite of Norito-first SDKs, REST/gRPC gateways, and deterministic builders that let teams integrate without learning low-level ledger internals.
terms.definition: The suite of Norito-first SDKs, REST/gRPC gateways, and deterministic builders that let teams integrate without learning low-level ledger internals.

terms.title: DSID
terms.summary: A UUID-style identifier assigned to every data space, used for routing, policy lookup, and cross-space access control.
terms.definition: A UUID-style identifier assigned to every data space, used for routing, policy lookup, and cross-space access control.

terms.title: Dual-Sig
terms.summary: A policy pattern requiring two distinct signatures - often offline plus online or regulator plus operator - to authorize sensitive transactions.
terms.definition: A policy pattern requiring two distinct signatures - often offline plus online or regulator plus operator - to authorize sensitive transactions.

terms.title: Economic Model
terms.summary: The XOR-denominated fee, reward, and bonding framework that harmonizes incentives across public and private data spaces.
terms.definition: The XOR-denominated fee, reward, and bonding framework that harmonizes incentives across public and private data spaces.

terms.title: Ed25519
terms.summary: The default signature scheme for end users and public DA samples, chosen for speed and wide tooling support.
terms.definition: The default signature scheme for end users and public DA samples, chosen for speed and wide tooling support.

terms.title: Epoch Beacon
terms.summary: The randomness source derived from VRF aggregates each epoch, feeding leader rotation and other sortition processes.
terms.definition: The randomness source derived from VRF aggregates each epoch, feeding leader rotation and other sortition processes.

terms.title: Erasure-Coded Kura
terms.summary: The historical storage (Kura) extended with Reed - Solomon coding so archived blocks stay recoverable even with partial failures.
terms.definition: The historical storage (Kura) extended with Reed - Solomon coding so archived blocks stay recoverable even with partial failures.

terms.title: Erasure-Coded WSV
terms.summary: The World State View snapshots protected by erasure coding, enabling resilient state recovery across validators.
terms.definition: The World State View snapshots protected by erasure coding, enabling resilient state recovery across validators.

terms.title: Execution
terms.summary: The IVM phase where admitted instructions mutate the World State View under deterministic gas and syscall rules.
terms.definition: The IVM phase where admitted instructions mutate the World State View under deterministic gas and syscall rules.

terms.title: Exit Caches
terms.summary: SoraNet components that hold recent ciphertexts near egress points, smoothing traffic and hiding timing correlations.
terms.definition: SoraNet components that hold recent ciphertexts near egress points, smoothing traffic and hiding timing correlations.

terms.title: Exposure
terms.summary: The final lifecycle step where receipts, Merkle proofs, and ISO-aligned outputs are delivered back to users and connectors.
terms.definition: The final lifecycle step where receipts, Merkle proofs, and ISO-aligned outputs are delivered back to users and connectors.

terms.title: FASTPQ
terms.summary: SORA Nexus's zk-STARK proof system that captures Iroha Special Instructions with high throughput and post-quantum security.
terms.definition: SORA Nexus's zk-STARK proof system that captures Iroha Special Instructions with high throughput and post-quantum security.

terms.title: FASTPQ Constraint System
terms.summary: The AIR describing how ledger state transitions, Merkle paths, and balance updates must satisfy algebraic constraints before proving.
terms.definition: The AIR describing how ledger state transitions, Merkle paths, and balance updates must satisfy algebraic constraints before proving.

terms.title: FASTPQ End-to-End Example
terms.summary: The reference workflow showing how transfers, SMT updates, and proofs compose from trace commitment to verifier checks.
terms.definition: The reference workflow showing how transfers, SMT updates, and proofs compose from trace commitment to verifier checks.

terms.title: FASTPQ Proof Composition
terms.summary: The ordered phases - trace commitment, challenge derivation, DEEP-FRI folding, and Merkle openings - that create a FASTPQ proof.
terms.definition: The ordered phases - trace commitment, challenge derivation, DEEP-FRI folding, and Merkle openings - that create a FASTPQ proof.

terms.title: FASTPQ zk-STARK Proofs
terms.summary: Zero-knowledge proofs produced per data space or lane to attest to execution correctness without revealing private payloads.
terms.definition: Zero-knowledge proofs produced per data space or lane to attest to execution correctness without revealing private payloads.

terms.title: FASTPQ-ISI Proofs
terms.summary: Proof bundles scoped to specific Iroha Special Instructions, allowing granular verification and aggregation per lane.
terms.definition: Proof bundles scoped to specific Iroha Special Instructions, allowing granular verification and aggregation per lane.

terms.title: Fiat-Shamir Transcript
terms.summary: The hashed conversation log that records each commitment and challenge during proof generation, keeping the prover honest.
terms.definition: The hashed conversation log that records each commitment and challenge during proof generation, keeping the prover honest.

terms.title: Fiat-Shamir Transform
terms.summary: The process of converting FASTPQ's interactive protocol into a non-interactive one by hashing prior messages for randomness.
terms.definition: The process of converting FASTPQ's interactive protocol into a non-interactive one by hashing prior messages for randomness.

terms.title: Fixed-Size Cells
terms.summary: Uniform packet sizes in SoraNet that equalize traffic fingerprints and resist traffic analysis.
terms.definition: Uniform packet sizes in SoraNet that equalize traffic fingerprints and resist traffic analysis.

terms.title: Gas Tables
terms.summary: Versioned, audited cost schedules that assign deterministic TEU prices to every syscall and instruction inside the IVM.
terms.definition: Versioned, audited cost schedules that assign deterministic TEU prices to every syscall and instruction inside the IVM.

terms.title: Gateways
terms.summary: Stateless admission points that accept signed Norito payloads, apply basic checks, and route them to the proper data space.
terms.definition: Stateless admission points that accept signed Norito payloads, apply basic checks, and route them to the proper data space.

terms.title: Geo-Redundancy
terms.summary: Operational guidance for running validators, provers, and storage nodes across multiple regions to survive localized outages.
terms.definition: Operational guidance for running validators, provers, and storage nodes across multiple regions to survive localized outages.

terms.title: Goldilocks Field
terms.summary: The prime field used by Poseidon2 and FASTPQ's AIR so constraints map efficiently onto modern hardware.
terms.definition: The prime field used by Poseidon2 and FASTPQ's AIR so constraints map efficiently onto modern hardware.

terms.title: GOST Suites
terms.summary: Governance-selectable Russian cryptographic algorithms (SM2/3/4 equivalents) for jurisdictions that require national standards.
terms.definition: Governance-selectable Russian cryptographic algorithms (SM2/3/4 equivalents) for jurisdictions that require national standards.

terms.title: Governance Surfaces
terms.summary: The enumerated areas - config files, parameter sets, attestation policies - through which the network can evolve without forking.
terms.definition: The enumerated areas - config files, parameter sets, attestation policies - through which the network can evolve without forking.

terms.title: Governed Manifest
terms.summary: The hashed package of binaries, ABI versions, and activation slots that defines a runtime upgrade proposal.
terms.definition: The hashed package of binaries, ABI versions, and activation slots that defines a runtime upgrade proposal.

terms.title: gRPC Gateways
terms.summary: Binary RPC interfaces exposing Norito-first semantics for high-performance integrations that prefer typed protobuf APIs.
terms.definition: Binary RPC interfaces exposing Norito-first semantics for high-performance integrations that prefer typed protobuf APIs.

terms.title: Halo2 Circuits
terms.summary: Zero-knowledge circuits (PLONKish flavor) used for privacy transactions, offering succinct proofs for shielded asset flows.
terms.definition: Zero-knowledge circuits (PLONKish flavor) used for privacy transactions, offering succinct proofs for shielded asset flows.

terms.title: Halo2-IPA Proofs
terms.summary: Halo2 circuits paired with inner product argument commitments to keep verification costs logarithmic for shielded flows.
terms.definition: Halo2 circuits paired with inner product argument commitments to keep verification costs logarithmic for shielded flows.

terms.title: Hybrid PQ Handshake
terms.summary: SoraNet's combination of Curve25519 and Kyber768 during session setup, giving classical and post-quantum security simultaneously.
terms.definition: SoraNet's combination of Curve25519 and Kyber768 during session setup, giving classical and post-quantum security simultaneously.

terms.title: Interbank Settlement
terms.summary: A Nexus use case where regulated data spaces host RTGS-style payment flows with deterministic finality and auditability.
terms.definition: A Nexus use case where regulated data spaces host RTGS-style payment flows with deterministic finality and auditability.

terms.title: IPA Commitments
terms.summary: Polynomial commitments based on inner product arguments, employed in Halo2 privacy proofs to verify tables efficiently.
terms.definition: Polynomial commitments based on inner product arguments, employed in Halo2 privacy proofs to verify tables efficiently.

terms.title: Iroha Config
terms.summary: The canonical configuration file (`iroha_config`) that holds lane counts, cryptography switches, and other network parameters.
terms.definition: The canonical configuration file (`iroha_config`) that holds lane counts, cryptography switches, and other network parameters.

terms.title: Iroha Virtual Machine (IVM)
terms.summary: The Iroha Virtual Machine, a purpose-built deterministic runtime that executes Kotodama bytecode with typed ABIs and fixed gas.
terms.definition: The Iroha Virtual Machine, a purpose-built deterministic runtime that executes Kotodama bytecode with typed ABIs and fixed gas.

terms.title: ISO 20022
terms.summary: The global financial messaging standard that Nexus aligns with for payment, securities, and FX data models.
terms.definition: The global financial messaging standard that Nexus aligns with for payment, securities, and FX data models.

terms.title: ISO 20022 Alignment
terms.summary: The deterministic mapping of ISO 20022 message fields to Norito structures so banks can integrate without custom adapters.
terms.definition: The deterministic mapping of ISO 20022 message fields to Norito structures so banks can integrate without custom adapters.

terms.title: ISO 20022 Connectors
terms.summary: Gateway components that translate ISO 20022 payloads into Nexus transactions and return receipts back into banking flows.
terms.definition: Gateway components that translate ISO 20022 payloads into Nexus transactions and return receipts back into banking flows.

terms.title: IVM Bytecode
terms.summary: The compiled Kotodama program format (.to files) containing headers, ABI versions, and vector tables for IVM execution.
terms.definition: The compiled Kotodama program format (.to files) containing headers, ABI versions, and vector tables for IVM execution.

terms.title: Kaigi
terms.summary: The real-time conferencing product managed on-ledger, with governance for rooms, relays, and usage accounting.
terms.definition: The real-time conferencing product managed on-ledger, with governance for rooms, relays, and usage accounting.

terms.title: Kotodama
terms.summary: The strongly typed programming model and tooling that compiles into IVM bytecode for deterministic smart contracts.
terms.definition: The strongly typed programming model and tooling that compiles into IVM bytecode for deterministic smart contracts.

terms.title: Kotodama Bytecode
terms.summary: The low-level output of Kotodama compilers, packing opcodes, pointer tables, and gas ceilings enforced by the IVM.
terms.definition: The low-level output of Kotodama compilers, packing opcodes, pointer tables, and gas ceilings enforced by the IVM.

terms.title: Kotodama Runtime
terms.summary: The toolchain that validates Kotodama contracts, ensuring pointer ABIs and gas tables are compatible before deployment.
terms.definition: The toolchain that validates Kotodama contracts, ensuring pointer ABIs and gas tables are compatible before deployment.

terms.title: Kura
terms.summary: The append-only history store in Iroha 3 that records every committed block alongside erasure-coded redundancy.
terms.definition: The append-only history store in Iroha 3 that records every committed block alongside erasure-coded redundancy.

terms.title: Kyber768
terms.summary: The lattice-based KEM used in SoraNet's hybrid handshake to future-proof against quantum adversaries.
terms.definition: The lattice-based KEM used in SoraNet's hybrid handshake to future-proof against quantum adversaries.

terms.title: Lambda Exit
terms.summary: The throughput threshold that triggers deterministic lane splits when demand exceeds configured capacity.
terms.definition: The throughput threshold that triggers deterministic lane splits when demand exceeds configured capacity.

terms.title: Lambda Floor
terms.summary: The lower-load threshold that allows lanes to fuse, reducing overhead when traffic drops.
terms.definition: The lower-load threshold that allows lanes to fuse, reducing overhead when traffic drops.

terms.title: Lane and DA Budgets
terms.summary: The combined constraints governing how much transaction work and DA sampling a slot may perform.
terms.definition: The combined constraints governing how much transaction work and DA sampling a slot may perform.

terms.title: Lane Finality
terms.summary: The target that each lane's SUMERAGI pipeline reaches ~1-second confirmation before merge ordering.
terms.definition: The target that each lane's SUMERAGI pipeline reaches ~1-second confirmation before merge ordering.

terms.title: Lane Fusion
terms.summary: The deterministic process of collapsing multiple lanes when aggregate load falls below lambda_floor, preserving history.
terms.definition: The deterministic process of collapsing multiple lanes when aggregate load falls below lambda_floor, preserving history.

terms.title: Lane Proofs
terms.summary: Aggregated FASTPQ or DA proofs scoped per lane, allowing committees to verify execution efficiently.
terms.definition: Aggregated FASTPQ or DA proofs scoped per lane, allowing committees to verify execution efficiently.

terms.title: Lane Split
terms.summary: The act of doubling lanes once lambda_exit is exceeded, enabling horizontal scaling without rewriting history.
terms.definition: The act of doubling lanes once lambda_exit is exceeded, enabling horizontal scaling without rewriting history.

terms.title: Lane TEU Budget
terms.summary: The per-lane compute allowance (~20,000 TEU/s default) that keeps resource usage predictable.
terms.definition: The per-lane compute allowance (~20,000 TEU/s default) that keeps resource usage predictable.

terms.title: Lane-Scoped Recovery
terms.summary: SoraNet mechanisms that rebuild state for a single lane without halting the entire network.
terms.definition: SoraNet mechanisms that rebuild state for a single lane without halting the entire network.

terms.title: Lane-Scoped State
terms.summary: State shards maintained per lane (especially in SoraNet) to localize failures and simplify recovery.
terms.definition: State shards maintained per lane (especially in SoraNet) to localize failures and simplify recovery.

terms.title: Lanes
terms.summary: Parallel execution tracks that process transactions independently before a merge ledger orders their outputs.
terms.definition: Parallel execution tracks that process transactions independently before a merge ledger orders their outputs.

terms.title: Locked QC
terms.summary: The highest quorum certificate a validator is currently locked on, enforcing HotStuff-style safety rules.
terms.definition: The highest quorum certificate a validator is currently locked on, enforcing HotStuff-style safety rules.

terms.title: Memory Model
terms.summary: The IVM's segmented memory rules (code, heap, stack, IO) with strict bounds and Merkle commitments for traceability.
terms.definition: The IVM's segmented memory rules (code, heap, stack, IO) with strict bounds and Merkle commitments for traceability.

terms.title: Merge Ledger
terms.summary: The lightweight ordering layer that sequences finalized lane tips into a single global history.
terms.definition: The lightweight ordering layer that sequences finalized lane tips into a single global history.

terms.title: Merkle Commitments
terms.summary: Poseidon2-based Merkle roots over memory, registers, or storage that allow succinct verification of state changes.
terms.definition: Poseidon2-based Merkle roots over memory, registers, or storage that allow succinct verification of state changes.

terms.title: ML-DSA-87
terms.summary: The post-quantum signature suite used for consensus votes, data-space attestations, and private-domain proofs.
terms.definition: The post-quantum signature suite used for consensus votes, data-space attestations, and private-domain proofs.

terms.title: Multisig
terms.summary: Nexus's flexible signing model where different schemes (Ed25519, ML-DSA-87, etc.) can be mixed in m-of-n policies.
terms.definition: Nexus's flexible signing model where different schemes (Ed25519, ML-DSA-87, etc.) can be mixed in m-of-n policies.

terms.title: Must-Serve Slice
terms.summary: The fairness rule requiring any data space with pending work to get scheduled within a bounded number of slots.
terms.definition: The fairness rule requiring any data space with pending work to get scheduled within a bounded number of slots.

terms.title: NEW_VIEW
terms.summary: The SUMERAGI message that proves a validator has seen sufficient votes to advance to the next proposal round.
terms.definition: The SUMERAGI message that proves a validator has seen sufficient votes to advance to the next proposal round.

terms.title: Nexus Account Structure
terms.summary: The canonical binary layout of account identifiers, including network flags, DSID, domain, name, multisig metadata, and checksum.
terms.definition: The canonical binary layout of account identifiers, including network flags, DSID, domain, name, multisig metadata, and checksum.

terms.title: Norito
terms.summary: The canonical serialization language for commands, receipts, and state, ensuring all tooling speaks a single schema.
terms.definition: The canonical serialization language for commands, receipts, and state, ensuring all tooling speaks a single schema.

terms.title: Norito Codec
terms.summary: The implementation that encodes/decodes Norito TLV structures and streams data for storage or networking layers.
terms.definition: The implementation that encodes/decodes Norito TLV structures and streams data for storage or networking layers.

terms.title: Norito Receipts
terms.summary: Structured execution receipts generated by Norito, containing hashes, proofs, and state deltas for auditing.
terms.definition: Structured execution receipts generated by Norito, containing hashes, proofs, and state deltas for auditing.

terms.title: Norito Streaming
terms.summary: The process of chunking Norito payloads for SoraFS/SoraNet transport with deterministic framing.
terms.definition: The process of chunking Norito payloads for SoraFS/SoraNet transport with deterministic framing.

terms.title: Norito TLV
terms.summary: The typed-length-value format underlying Norito messages, enabling unambiguous parsing inside the IVM.
terms.definition: The typed-length-value format underlying Norito messages, enabling unambiguous parsing inside the IVM.

terms.title: Norito-First APIs
terms.summary: Developer interfaces that expose ledger functionality directly in Norito semantics, reducing translation bugs.
terms.definition: Developer interfaces that expose ledger functionality directly in Norito semantics, reducing translation bugs.

terms.title: NPoS Variant
terms.summary: A committee selection option where validators are chosen via Nominated Proof of Stake with VRF sortition.
terms.definition: A committee selection option where validators are chosen via Nominated Proof of Stake with VRF sortition.

terms.title: Nullifiers
terms.summary: Hash-derived tags in shielded transfers that prevent double-spending by marking commitments as spent once revealed.
terms.definition: Hash-derived tags in shielded transfers that prevent double-spending by marking commitments as spent once revealed.

terms.title: Offline-Offline Transactions
terms.summary: Voucher-based transfers signed while disconnected, later reconciled through gateways with circuit breakers and revocation windows.
terms.definition: Voucher-based transfers signed while disconnected, later reconciled through gateways with circuit breakers and revocation windows.

terms.title: Parallel Lanes
terms.summary: The architectural pattern of running multiple lanes simultaneously to boost throughput without spawning new chains.
terms.definition: The architectural pattern of running multiple lanes simultaneously to boost throughput without spawning new chains.

terms.title: Parameter Sets
terms.summary: Versioned on-chain collections of cryptography choices, admission caps, and scheduler knobs that governance can update.
terms.definition: Versioned on-chain collections of cryptography choices, admission caps, and scheduler knobs that governance can update.

terms.title: Performance Targets
terms.summary: The published defaults (<=1 s lane finality, <=32 MB envelopes, etc.) guiding deployments toward predictable behavior.
terms.definition: The published defaults (<=1 s lane finality, <=32 MB envelopes, etc.) guiding deployments toward predictable behavior.

terms.title: PLONKish
terms.summary: A descriptor for the Halo2 circuit style that supports lookups and flexible gates, enabling efficient privacy proofs.
terms.definition: A descriptor for the Halo2 circuit style that supports lookups and flexible gates, enabling efficient privacy proofs.

terms.title: Pointer ABI
terms.summary: The typed handle interface that prevents contracts from misusing identifiers by encoding domain-specific types into pointers.
terms.definition: The typed handle interface that prevents contracts from misusing identifiers by encoding domain-specific types into pointers.

terms.title: Poseidon2
terms.summary: The hash function optimized for zero-knowledge circuits, used extensively in FASTPQ commitments and SMTs.
terms.definition: The hash function optimized for zero-knowledge circuits, used extensively in FASTPQ commitments and SMTs.

terms.title: Pre-Authorized Vouchers
terms.summary: Signed value chits bound to a snapshot and revocation window, enabling offline-offline payments with later reconciliation.
terms.definition: Signed value chits bound to a snapshot and revocation window, enabling offline-offline payments with later reconciliation.

terms.title: Privacy Transactions
terms.summary: Shielded flows that keep amounts and participants confidential via Halo2 circuits, commitments, and nullifiers.
terms.definition: Shielded flows that keep amounts and participants confidential via Halo2 circuits, commitments, and nullifiers.

terms.title: Private Data Spaces
terms.summary: Permissioned domains where data and proofs remain within the operator's trust boundary, using ML-DSA attestations for DA.
terms.definition: Permissioned domains where data and proofs remain within the operator's trust boundary, using ML-DSA attestations for DA.

terms.title: Proof Systems
terms.summary: The combination of FASTPQ STARKs, Halo2 circuits, and supporting protocols that provide verifiable execution and privacy.
terms.definition: The combination of FASTPQ STARKs, Halo2 circuits, and supporting protocols that provide verifiable execution and privacy.

terms.title: Proof Verification Budget
terms.summary: The per-slot time allocation (100 - 200 ms typical) reserved for lane committees to check proofs without falling behind.
terms.definition: The per-slot time allocation (100 - 200 ms typical) reserved for lane committees to check proofs without falling behind.

terms.title: Propose-Validate-Vote-Commit
terms.summary: The SUMERAGI pipeline stages that drive HotStuff-style consensus with deterministic leader rotation and locking.
terms.definition: The SUMERAGI pipeline stages that drive HotStuff-style consensus with deterministic leader rotation and locking.

terms.title: Provers
terms.summary: Actors (often GPU-accelerated) that generate FASTPQ or DA proofs and deliver them within the configured latency budget.
terms.definition: Actors (often GPU-accelerated) that generate FASTPQ or DA proofs and deliver them within the configured latency budget.

terms.title: Public Data Spaces
terms.summary: Open participation domains where DA sampling is performed publicly and Ed25519 signatures attest to availability.
terms.definition: Open participation domains where DA sampling is performed publicly and Ed25519 signatures attest to availability.

terms.title: Quorum Certificate
terms.summary: The aggregated signature set (>=2f+1) that certifies a proposal, underpinning SUMERAGI's safety guarantees.
terms.definition: The aggregated signature set (>=2f+1) that certifies a proposal, underpinning SUMERAGI's safety guarantees.

terms.title: Reed-Solomon
terms.summary: The erasure-coding scheme used in SoraFS for both row and column parity, ensuring any k shards reconstruct the envelope.
terms.definition: The erasure-coding scheme used in SoraFS for both row and column parity, ensuring any k shards reconstruct the envelope.

terms.title: REST Gateways
terms.summary: HTTP interfaces that expose Norito-first APIs for developers who prefer REST semantics over gRPC.
terms.definition: HTTP interfaces that expose Norito-first APIs for developers who prefer REST semantics over gRPC.

terms.title: Revocation Windows
terms.summary: Bounded time intervals during which off-chain vouchers can be canceled if reconciliation uncovers fraud.
terms.definition: Bounded time intervals during which off-chain vouchers can be canceled if reconciliation uncovers fraud.

terms.title: Rolling Upgrades
terms.summary: Operational practice of upgrading validators and provers in waves while keeping lanes live, aided by manifests and telemetry.
terms.definition: Operational practice of upgrading validators and provers in waves while keeping lanes live, aided by manifests and telemetry.

terms.title: RTGS Modernization
terms.summary: A targeted use case where central banks run real-time gross settlement on Nexus with deterministic policy controls.
terms.definition: A targeted use case where central banks run real-time gross settlement on Nexus with deterministic policy controls.

terms.title: Runtime Upgrades
terms.summary: Governed changes to binaries, ABIs, or parameters that are staged, verified, and activated atomically at an agreed slot.
terms.definition: Governed changes to binaries, ABIs, or parameters that are staged, verified, and activated atomically at an agreed slot.

terms.title: SCALE
terms.summary: Parity's serialization format mentioned as explicitly excluded from production Nexus paths to avoid ambiguity.
terms.definition: Parity's serialization format mentioned as explicitly excluded from production Nexus paths to avoid ambiguity.

terms.title: SDKs
terms.summary: Language toolkits (mobile, web, server) that wrap Norito schemas, ISO helpers, and offline flows for application builders.
terms.definition: Language toolkits (mobile, web, server) that wrap Norito schemas, ISO helpers, and offline flows for application builders.

terms.title: Secp256k1
terms.summary: The legacy signature scheme kept for interoperability with ecosystems that still rely on it.
terms.definition: The legacy signature scheme kept for interoperability with ecosystems that still rely on it.

terms.title: Seed Beacon
terms.summary: The randomness derivation combining previous epoch entropy and BLAKE2b hashing to select leaders fairly.
terms.definition: The randomness derivation combining previous epoch entropy and BLAKE2b hashing to select leaders fairly.

terms.title: SHA-2
terms.summary: A legacy hash suite retained for interoperability with existing systems and regulatory requirements.
terms.definition: A legacy hash suite retained for interoperability with existing systems and regulatory requirements.

terms.title: SHA-3
terms.summary: A Keccak-based hash option for domains needing standardization beyond Poseidon2.
terms.definition: A Keccak-based hash option for domains needing standardization beyond Poseidon2.

terms.title: Shielded Roots
terms.summary: Merkle roots of the shielded commitment trees that prove privacy balances updated correctly.
terms.definition: Merkle roots of the shielded commitment trees that prove privacy balances updated correctly.

terms.title: Shielded Transfers
terms.summary: Privacy-preserving asset moves that use commitments, nullifiers, and Halo2 proofs to hide values while keeping auditability.
terms.definition: Privacy-preserving asset moves that use commitments, nullifiers, and Halo2 proofs to hide values while keeping auditability.

terms.title: SignedBlockWire
terms.summary: The versioned wire format for distributing and persisting blocks, including headers, signatures, and Norito payload references.
terms.definition: The versioned wire format for distributing and persisting blocks, including headers, signatures, and Norito payload references.

terms.title: Slashing
terms.summary: The penalty framework that confiscates bonds or XOR rewards when validators double-sign or violate protocol rules.
terms.definition: The penalty framework that confiscates bonds or XOR rewards when validators double-sign or violate protocol rules.

terms.title: SM2
terms.summary: The Chinese national elliptic-curve signature suite available via governance for compliant deployments.
terms.definition: The Chinese national elliptic-curve signature suite available via governance for compliant deployments.

terms.title: SM3
terms.summary: The companion hash function from the Chinese SM cryptographic family.
terms.definition: The companion hash function from the Chinese SM cryptographic family.

terms.title: SM4
terms.summary: The Chinese block cipher offered for national deployments needing SM2/3 compatibility.
terms.definition: The Chinese block cipher offered for national deployments needing SM2/3 compatibility.

terms.title: SORA Nexus
terms.summary: The single logical ledger built on Hyperledger Iroha 3 that unifies private data spaces, public domains, and modern cryptography.
terms.definition: The single logical ledger built on Hyperledger Iroha 3 that unifies private data spaces, public domains, and modern cryptography.

terms.title: Soracles
terms.summary: Deterministic oracle actors governed like data spaces, complete with onboarding, rate limits, and proof budgets.
terms.definition: Deterministic oracle actors governed like data spaces, complete with onboarding, rate limits, and proof budgets.

terms.title: SoraFS
terms.summary: The decentralized storage and erasure-coding layer that handles lane envelopes, DA proofs, and retry policies.
terms.definition: The decentralized storage and erasure-coding layer that handles lane envelopes, DA proofs, and retry policies.

terms.title: SoraNet
terms.summary: The privacy overlay and deterministic CDN that uses three-hop QUIC circuits, hybrid PQ handshakes, and blinded metadata for data delivery.
terms.definition: The privacy overlay and deterministic CDN that uses three-hop QUIC circuits, hybrid PQ handshakes, and blinded metadata for data delivery.

terms.title: Sovereign Data Spaces
terms.summary: Data spaces that let entities maintain jurisdictional control over privacy, routing, and compliance while sharing the global ledger.
terms.definition: Data spaces that let entities maintain jurisdictional control over privacy, routing, and compliance while sharing the global ledger.

terms.title: STARK
terms.summary: The transparent proof system underpinning FASTPQ, providing post-quantum security without trusted setup.
terms.definition: The transparent proof system underpinning FASTPQ, providing post-quantum security without trusted setup.

terms.title: STARK Security Budget
terms.summary: The parameter sizing (blow-up factors, query counts, grinding) that keeps FASTPQ proofs at >=128-bit soundness.
terms.definition: The parameter sizing (blow-up factors, query counts, grinding) that keeps FASTPQ proofs at >=128-bit soundness.

terms.title: Start-Time Fair Queuing (SFQ)
terms.summary: Start-Time Fair Queuing, the scheduler that orders work by virtual finish times while enforcing TEU and age constraints.
terms.definition: Start-Time Fair Queuing, the scheduler that orders work by virtual finish times while enforcing TEU and age constraints.

terms.title: State Application
terms.summary: The deterministic process of applying validated instructions to the World State View after consensus confirms a block.
terms.definition: The deterministic process of applying validated instructions to the World State View after consensus confirms a block.

terms.title: Submission
terms.summary: The first step of the transaction lifecycle where signed Norito instructions enter the network through gateways.
terms.definition: The first step of the transaction lifecycle where signed Norito instructions enter the network through gateways.

terms.title: Sumeragi
terms.summary: The BFT consensus protocol used by Iroha 3, adapted with deterministic leader rotation and locking rules.
terms.definition: The BFT consensus protocol used by Iroha 3, adapted with deterministic leader rotation and locking rules.

terms.title: Sumeragi Consensus
terms.summary: The formal HotStuff-style guarantees - safety, liveness, and QC intersection - baked into the SUMERAGI pipeline.
terms.definition: The formal HotStuff-style guarantees - safety, liveness, and QC intersection - baked into the SUMERAGI pipeline.

terms.title: SUMERAGI Pipeline
terms.summary: The multi-stage HotStuff-like process in Iroha 3 that sequences proposals, votes, and commits per lane.
terms.definition: The multi-stage HotStuff-like process in Iroha 3 that sequences proposals, votes, and commits per lane.

terms.title: Syscalls
terms.summary: The limited, 8-bit-indexed entry points exposed by the IVM for interactions like hashing or storage, each with deterministic gas cost.
terms.definition: The limited, 8-bit-indexed entry points exposed by the IVM for interactions like hashing or storage, each with deterministic gas cost.

terms.title: Taikai
terms.summary: The streaming and data pipeline platform governed on-ledger, supporting Norito streaming, telemetry, and slashing for misbehavior.
terms.definition: The streaming and data pipeline platform governed on-ledger, supporting Norito streaming, telemetry, and slashing for misbehavior.

terms.title: Telemetry
terms.summary: The observability feeds - lane latency, DA failures, breaker status - that operators monitor to keep Nexus healthy.
terms.definition: The observability feeds - lane latency, DA failures, breaker status - that operators monitor to keep Nexus healthy.

terms.title: Three-Hop QUIC Circuits
terms.summary: SoraNet's onion-style routing pattern using QUIC, providing low-latency privacy with fixed hop counts.
terms.definition: SoraNet's onion-style routing pattern using QUIC, providing low-latency privacy with fixed hop counts.

terms.title: Tokenized Assets
terms.summary: A use case where real-world assets are issued in data spaces with deterministic policy, proofs, and ISO-aligned connectors.
terms.definition: A use case where real-world assets are issued in data spaces with deterministic policy, proofs, and ISO-aligned connectors.

terms.title: Torii
terms.summary: The Norito-native gateway that streams events, receipts, and telemetry to clients via REST, SSE, or gRPC.
terms.definition: The Norito-native gateway that streams events, receipts, and telemetry to clients via REST, SSE, or gRPC.

terms.title: Transaction Execution Units (TEU)
terms.summary: Transaction Execution Units, the resource metric that measures instruction cost, bandwidth, and storage to drive scheduling and fees.
terms.definition: Transaction Execution Units, the resource metric that measures instruction cost, bandwidth, and storage to drive scheduling and fees.

terms.title: Transaction Lifecycle
terms.summary: The six-stage flow - submission, admission, execution, aggregation, consensus, exposure - that every Nexus transaction follows.
terms.definition: The six-stage flow - submission, admission, execution, aggregation, consensus, exposure - that every Nexus transaction follows.

terms.title: Triggers
terms.summary: On-ledger automation objects composed of condition, action, and budget fields, enabling schedules or reactions without off-chain cron jobs.
terms.definition: On-ledger automation objects composed of condition, action, and budget fields, enabling schedules or reactions without off-chain cron jobs.

terms.title: Two-Dimensional Erasure Coding
terms.summary: The matrix-style Reed - Solomon scheme (rows and columns) SoraFS uses to ensure any subset of shards can rebuild the original data.
terms.definition: The matrix-style Reed - Solomon scheme (rows and columns) SoraFS uses to ensure any subset of shards can rebuild the original data.

terms.title: VRF Aggregate
terms.summary: The combined verifiable random function output from committees, feeding epoch beacons and lane-specific randomness.
terms.definition: The combined verifiable random function output from committees, feeding epoch beacons and lane-specific randomness.

terms.title: VRF Sortition
terms.summary: The method of drawing validator committees by having candidates prove, via VRF, that their random output meets a threshold.
terms.definition: The method of drawing validator committees by having candidates prove, via VRF, that their random output meets a threshold.

terms.title: World State View (WSV)
terms.summary: World State View, the canonical state database that holds current balances, metadata, and trigger definitions.
terms.definition: World State View, the canonical state database that holds current balances, metadata, and trigger definitions.

terms.title: XOR Bonds
terms.summary: Stake deposits in XOR that governance proposals or data-space onboardings must lock to align incentives.
terms.definition: Stake deposits in XOR that governance proposals or data-space onboardings must lock to align incentives.

terms.title: XOR Fee Equilibrium
terms.summary: The economic model that balances lane demand, TEU costs, and fee floors so XOR rewards stay predictable.
terms.definition: The economic model that balances lane demand, TEU costs, and fee floors so XOR rewards stay predictable.

terms.title: XOR Utility
terms.summary: The multi-role nature of XOR as fee token, settlement asset, collateral, and governance bond across data spaces.
terms.definition: The multi-role nature of XOR as fee token, settlement asset, collateral, and governance bond across data spaces.

terms.title: ZK DA Proofs
terms.summary: Zero-knowledge proofs that bind erasure-coded shards to block commitments, proving availability without revealing private data.
terms.definition: Zero-knowledge proofs that bind erasure-coded shards to block commitments, proving availability without revealing private data.

terms.title: ZK-Backed Access Tickets
terms.summary: Proof-carrying credentials in SoraNet that grant network access while obscuring user identity or route.
terms.definition: Proof-carrying credentials in SoraNet that grant network access while obscuring user identity or route.

terms.title: ZK-STARK vs. STARK
terms.summary: The Nexus clarification that FASTPQ can run in audit (non-zk) or privacy (zk) modes while sharing the same verifier logic.
terms.definition: The Nexus clarification that FASTPQ can run in audit (non-zk) or privacy (zk) modes while sharing the same verifier logic.
